claim: Hanahan and Weinberg's seminal paper 'The Hallmarks of Cancer' was revised in 2011 to include deregulating cellular energetics and evasion of immune destruction.
source: Hanahan and Weinberg's seminal paper 'The Hallmarks of Cancer' was revised in 2011 to include deregulating cellular energetics and evasion of immune destruction (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011.

claim: Tumors fuel their rapid growth and proliferation with aerobic glycolysis.
source: Tumors fuel their rapid growth and proliferation with aerobic glycolysis, a process initially described by Otto Warburg in which cells undergo glycolysis even in the presence of oxygen (Lebelo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lebelo et al., 2019, and draws on established scientific knowledge about the Warburg effect.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis is a process in which cells undergo glycolysis even in the presence of oxygen.
source: Tumors fuel their rapid growth and proliferation with aerobic glycolysis, a process initially described by Otto Warburg in which cells undergo glycolysis even in the presence of oxygen (Lebelo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lebelo et al., 2019, and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis was initially described by Otto Warburg.
source: Tumors fuel their rapid growth and proliferation with aerobic glycolysis, a process initially described by Otto Warburg in which cells undergo glycolysis even in the presence of oxygen (Lebelo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lebelo et al., 2019, and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis is less energetically efficient than oxidation that occurs in most mature tissues.
source: Although less energetically efficient than oxidation that occurs in most mature tissues, aerobic glycolysis shuttles intermediates into biosynthetic pathways to make amino acids, nucleotides, fatty acids and other macromolecules to support rapid anabolic growth (Pavlova and Thompson, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pavlova and Thompson, 2016, and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis shuttles intermediates into biosynthetic pathways to make amino acids, nucleotides, fatty acids and other macromolecules to support rapid anabolic growth.
source: Although less energetically efficient than oxidation that occurs in most mature tissues, aerobic glycolysis shuttles intermediates into biosynthetic pathways to make amino acids, nucleotides, fatty acids and other macromolecules to support rapid anabolic growth (Pavlova and Thompson, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pavlova and Thompson, 2016.

claim: Glucose and amino acids can be rapidly consumed while waste products accumulate as a consequence of aerobic glycolysis.
source: As a consequence, glucose and amino acids can be rapidly consumed while waste products accumulate.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the preceding discussion of aerobic glycolysis in tumors.

claim: Activated T cells undergo a metabolic switch from oxidative metabolism to aerobic glycolysis to proliferate and develop effector function.
source: Activated T cells also undergo a metabolic switch from oxidative metabolism to aerobic glycolysis to proliferate and develop effector function (Menk et al., 2018; Bantug et al., 2018a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Menk et al., 2018 and Bantug et al., 2018a.

claim: Rapid proliferation and acquisition of effector function are demanding processes that require precise metabolic re-wiring.
source: Rapid proliferation and acquisition of effector function are demanding processes that require precise metabolic re-wiring.
evidence: This claim represents established scientific knowledge about T cell metabolism.

claim: Failure of activated T cells to undergo metabolic re-wiring impairs effector function.
source: Failure of activated T cells to undergo metabolic re-wiring impairs effector function (Kouidhi et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kouidhi et al., 2017.

claim: T cell metabolism dictates effector function.
source: As T cell metabolism dictates effector function, it is now apparent that the effect of cancer cell metabolism on the tumor microenvironment (TME) may impair anti-tumor immunity, and these new hallmarks of cancer are therefore inextricably linked.
evidence: This claim represents established scientific knowledge and is inferred from the preceding discussion.

claim: The effect of cancer cell metabolism on the tumor microenvironment may impair anti-tumor immunity.
source: As T cell metabolism dictates effector function, it is now apparent that the effect of cancer cell metabolism on the tumor microenvironment (TME) may impair anti-tumor immunity, and these new hallmarks of cancer are therefore inextricably linked.
evidence: This claim is speculative and represents a hypothesis based on the preceding discussion.

claim: The new hallmarks of cancer (deregulating cellular energetics and evasion of immune destruction) are inextricably linked.
source: As T cell metabolism dictates effector function, it is now apparent that the effect of cancer cell metabolism on the tumor microenvironment (TME) may impair anti-tumor immunity, and these new hallmarks of cancer are therefore inextricably linked.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Baumeister et al., 2016, and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Adoptive cell transfer expands a patient's own T cells ex vivo to direct anti-tumor immunity when transfused back into the patient.
source: In contrast, ACT expands a patient's own T cells ex vivo to direct anti-tumor immunity when transfused back into the patient.

claim: Immune checkpoint blockade and adoptive cell transfer have shown great promise in many types of cancer and even produce long-lasting responses in some patients.

claim: Many patients fail to respond to immune checkpoint blockade and adoptive cell transfer therapies.

claim: Naïve T cells utilize a catabolic metabolism in which small amounts of glucose are used to generate ATP mainly through oxidative phosphorylation to support immune surveillance.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis allows T cells to build substrates needed for growth and proliferation and is essential for effector differentiation.
source: Although fewer ATP molecules are generated per glucose molecule, aerobic glycolysis allows T cells to build substrates needed for growth and proliferation and is essential for effector differentiation (Menk et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Menk et al., 2018.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis generates fewer ATP molecules per glucose molecule than oxidative phosphorylation.
source: Although fewer ATP molecules are generated per glucose molecule, aerobic glycolysis allows T cells to build substrates needed for growth and proliferation and is essential for effector differentiation (Menk et al., 2018).

claim: Metabolic reprogramming from catabolism to anabolism is initiated upon T Cell Receptor recognition of cognate antigen presented on major histocompatibility complex and with the help of CD28-mediated co-stimulation.
